name: Airbus A220-300
short_description: Modern single-aisle jet optimized for short-to-medium haul routes with state-of-the-art efficiency.
description: Originally developed by Bombardier as the CSeries, the Airbus A220-300 delivers exceptional efficiency, wide seats, and reduced environmental impact, perfectly suited for regional and transcontinental routes.
keyFeatures: Pratt & Whitney GTF Engines
Widest seats in the single-aisle market
Large overhead bins
Advanced composite wings

name: Airbus A310-300
short_description: Pioneering medium-to-long-range twin-engine wide-body jet liner.
description: The Airbus A310 was a major milestone for Airbus, featuring a two-crew glass cockpit, revolutionary digital avionics, and composite materials on a shorter wide-body frame derived from the A300.
keyFeatures: First wide-body two-crew glass cockpit
Carbon fiber composite tailfin
Transatlantic twin-engine pioneer

name: Airbus A320-200
short_description: The world's best-selling single-aisle commercial jet airliner family.
description: The A320 introduced digital fly-by-wire flight control systems to commercial aviation and remains the backbone of short- and medium-haul commercial fleets around the globe.
keyFeatures: Digital Fly-By-Wire control system
Side-stick flight controls
Containerized cargo loading system

name: Airbus A330-300
short_description: Versatile twin-engine wide-body aircraft popular on long-haul routes.
description: The Airbus A330-300 offers exceptional operational reliability and efficiency, filling long-haul routes seamlessly while offering operators high flexibility and twin-engine fuel savings.
keyFeatures: Twin-engine long-haul efficiency
Shared cockpit commonality with A340
Spacious 8-abreast economy layout

name: Airbus A340-600
short_description: Four-engine ultra-long-haul airliner known for its impressive length.
description: Once the world's longest commercial aircraft, the quad-engine A340-600 was built for long transoceanic routes without ETOPS restrictions, offering smooth rides and large passenger capacities.
keyFeatures: Quad-engine safety margin for oceanic routes
Extremely long fuselage design
Underfloor lavatory option

name: Airbus A350-900
short_description: Next-generation carbon-composite widebody built for ultra-long haul journeys.
description: Featuring a airframe constructed of over 50% carbon composites, curved winglets, and lower cabin pressure altitude, the A350 XWB sets modern standards in flight range, fuel efficiency, and passenger comfort.
keyFeatures: Carbon-fiber reinforced polymer (CFRP) body
Advanced aerodynamic winglets
Airspace cabin with lower cabin altitude

name: Airbus A380-800
short_description: The world's largest passenger airliner, featuring a full double-deck layout.
description: The flagship superjumbo of modern aviation, the A380-800 is the largest mass-produced passenger airliner ever built, famous for quiet flight cabins, onboard showers, and massive hub-to-hub seat capacity.
keyFeatures: Full-length double deck
Quiet cabin acoustic insulation
High-density megahub transport capability

name: Airbus A300-600R
short_description: The world's first twin-engine wide-body commercial airliner.
description: The pioneer that launched Airbus into global aviation dominance, the A300 proved that twin-engine widebodies could safely and efficiently replace older three- and four-engine jets on medium-to-long range routes.
keyFeatures: First wide-body twin-engine airliner
Pioneered composite structural components in commercial jets
Widely converted to dedicated long-life cargo freighters

name: Airbus A318-100
short_description: The smallest member of the original Airbus A320 family, nicknamed the 'Baby Bus'.
description: Designed for steep approaches and short-field performance, the A318 brought wide single-aisle comfort and full A320 fleet commonality to smaller regional routes and restricted airports.
keyFeatures: Certified for London City Airport steep approach operations
Tallest vertical stabilizer in the A320ceo family relative to fuselage
Full fly-by-wire commonality with the A320 family

name: Airbus A319-100
short_description: Popular shortened variant of the A320 offering long range and versatile performance.
description: The A319 shortened the baseline A320 fuselage by 3.7 meters while retaining the same wing fuel capacity, resulting in extended range and versatile performance popular on thin or high-altitude routes.
keyFeatures: Extended range performance compared to baseline A320
Popular choice for corporate private jet conversions (ACJ)
High altitude airport operation capabilities

name: Airbus A321-200
short_description: Stretched single-aisle flagship offering high seat capacity and economical flight operations.
description: Stretched by nearly 7 meters over the baseline A320, the A321-200 provides airlines with high passenger density and favorable seat-mile economics for trunk domestic routes.
keyFeatures: Stretched fuselage for high passenger throughput
Double-slotted trailing-edge flaps for low-speed handling
Containerized underfloor cargo hold loading

name: Airbus A321XLR
short_description: Extra Long Range single-aisle liner capable of flying transatlantic long-haul sectors.
description: The A321XLR represents the ultimate iteration of narrowbody range capability. Featuring a permanent Rear Center Tank (RCT) and a 101-tonne MTOW, it enables airlines to economically fly transatlantic and long thin point-to-point routes previously reserved for widebodies.
keyFeatures: Permanent integrated Rear Center Tank (RCT)
4,700 nm maximum range with single-aisle fuel burn efficiency
Airspace cabin layout with lie-flat business class capability

name: Boeing 717-200
short_description: Twin-engine short-range regional jet originally designed as the MD-95.
description: The Boeing 717 is a twin-engine, single-aisle commercial jet airliner designed specifically for the 100-seat regional market. Rebranded after Boeing acquired McDonnell Douglas, it gained a reputation for high reliability on frequent, short-haul routes.
keyFeatures: Rear-mounted Rolls-Royce BR715 engines
5-abreast economy seating layout
High reliability on short-turnaround regional routes

name: Boeing 737-800
short_description: The quintessential short-to-medium haul airliner of modern aviation history.
description: As the most widely produced variant of the Boeing 737 Next Generation family, the 737-800 is a staple of global airline fleets, renowned for low operating costs and high operational flexibility.
keyFeatures: Blended winglets for fuel efficiency
Boeing Sky Interior option
Flat-bottomed engine nacelles

name: Boeing 747-400
short_description: The legendary 'Queen of the Skies' featuring a prominent upper deck hump.
description: The Boeing 747-400 refined the iconic wide-body jumbo jet with glass cockpit technology, winglets, and improved engines, serving for decades as the premier long-haul flagship for airlines worldwide.
keyFeatures: Iconic double-deck hump upper section
Quad-engine performance with high payload capacity
First 747 variant with a two-crew glass cockpit

name: Boeing 757-200
short_description: High-performance single-aisle jet legendary for hot-and-high airport operations.
description: The Boeing 757-200 is famous for its exceptional thrust-to-weight ratio, allowing it to take off from short runways and high-altitude airports while carrying heavy payloads across transatlantic distances.
keyFeatures: Outstanding hot-and-high takeoff performance
Transatlantic range in a narrow-body frame
Common pilot type rating with the wide-body Boeing 767

name: Boeing 767-300ER
short_description: Workhorse wide-body twinjet that pioneered ETOPS transatlantic routes.
description: The Boeing 767-300ER was central to the expansion of long-range twin-engine flights across the Atlantic. Its 7-abreast 2-3-2 economy seating remains popular among passengers for giving everyone a seat near an aisle.
keyFeatures: Seven-abreast twin-aisle seating
Pioneered long-haul ETOPS overwater capabilities
Shared cockpit commonality with the Boeing 757

name: Boeing 777-300ER
short_description: The world's largest twin-engine long-haul commercial airliner.
description: Known as the 'Triple Seven', the Boeing 777-300ER combines massive twin-engine efficiency, high cargo capability, and extreme reliability, making it the primary long-haul flagship for airlines worldwide.
keyFeatures: GE90 engines — among the most powerful jet engines in commercial aviation
Raked wingtips for optimized aerodynamic efficiency
Six-wheel main landing gear trucks

name: Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner
short_description: Composite-built wide-body wide-range liner with electrochromic windows.
description: The Boeing 787-9 Dreamliner leverages composite material construction to deliver high fuel efficiency, lower cabin altitude pressures, higher humidity levels, and large electronically dimmable windows.
keyFeatures: Carbon-laminate composite fuselage structure
Electrochromic dimmable passenger windows
Chevron-patterned engine nacelles for noise reduction

name: Boeing 707-320C
short_description: The pioneer of commercial jet air travel that ushered in the Jet Age.
description: The Boeing 707 revolutionized passenger air travel in the late 1950s. Featuring swept wings and podded engines mounted underneath, it proved commercial jet transport was economically viable and established Boeing as a global commercial aviation leader.
keyFeatures: Pioneered the Jet Age for mainstream passenger transport
Swept wing design podded engine pod layout
Three-crew flight deck layout (Pilot, Co-Pilot, Flight Engineer)

name: Boeing 727-200
short_description: Trijet airliner famous for short runway capabilities and integrated airstairs.
description: The Boeing 727 was designed to service short runways and smaller airports without ground power units or jet bridges. Its rear-mounted trijet design, T-tail, and triple-slotted flaps gave it unprecedented short-field takeoff and landing performance.
keyFeatures: Rear S-duct intake for central third engine
Retractable ventral rear airstairs
High-lift triple-slotted flaps for short-field performance

name: Boeing 737 MAX 8
short_description: Fourth-generation 737 featuring LEAP-1B engines and split-scimitar winglets.
description: The Boeing 737 MAX 8 features larger CFM LEAP-1B engines, distinctive Advanced Technology winglets, and updated flight deck displays derived from the 787 Dreamliner, providing double-digit fuel efficiency improvements over the 737 NG.
keyFeatures: CFM LEAP-1B engines with chevrons on engine nacelles
Dual-feather Advanced Technology (AT) winglets
787-style widescreen glass cockpit displays

name: Boeing 777-9 (777X)
short_description: Boeing's flagship twinjet wide-body featuring folding composite wingtips.
description: The Boeing 777-9 is the largest twin-engine jetliner built to date. It introduces a high-aspect-ratio carbon composite wing with innovative folding wingtips, GE9X engines (the largest fan jet engines ever built), and wider internal cabin dimensions.
keyFeatures: Folding composite wingtips to fit existing airport gate dimensions
GE9X engines featuring 3D-printed fuel nozzles and ceramic matrix composites
Wider cabin architecture with enlarged windows inspired by the 787

name: Embraer E170
short_description: The founding model of Embraer's highly successful regional E-Jet family.
description: The E170 launched Embraer's double-bubble fuselage regional series, offering mainline passenger comforts like four-across seating with no middle seats and full-height stand-up cabins.
keyFeatures: Double-bubble cross-section for maximum shoulder room
2x2 seating layout with no middle seats
Fly-by-wire flight control system

name: Embraer E175
short_description: Dominant regional airliner optimized for US airline scope clauses.
description: Slightly stretched over the E170, the E175 became the gold standard for regional fleets across North America due to its alignment with US scope clause limits and low unit operating costs.
keyFeatures: Optimized capacity for US Scope Clause requirements
Extended angled winglets for fuel reduction
Spacious overhead bins for standard roller bags

name: Embraer E190
short_description: 100-seat regional jet bridging the gap between feeder and mainline aircraft.
description: Featuring a larger wing and more powerful GE CF34-10E engines than the E170/E175, the E190 extended regional carrier capabilities into mainstream point-to-point trunk routes.
keyFeatures: Steep approach approval for London City Airport
High cruising speed comparable to narrowbody mainliners
Dual underfloor cargo holds

name: Embraer E195
short_description: Largest model of the first-generation Embraer E-Jet family.
description: Stretched by 2.4 meters compared to the E190, the E195 targeted low-cost carriers looking for low trip costs on short-haul routes where narrow-body mainline aircraft were too large.
keyFeatures: Maximum seat capacity in the original E-Jet generation
Low seat-mile cost for regional operations
Shared type rating with the E190

name: Embraer E190-E2
short_description: Second-generation ultra-efficient regional jet with Geared Turbofan engines.
description: The E190-E2 upgrades the E190 with high-bypass Pratt & Whitney GTF engines, an all-new ultra-high-aspect-ratio wing, and closed-loop full fly-by-wire controls for double-digit fuel savings.
keyFeatures: Pratt & Whitney Geared Turbofan (GTF) propulsion
Ultra-high-aspect-ratio wing with no winglets
Full closed-loop fly-by-wire architecture

name: Embraer E195-E2
short_description: Embraer's flagship 'Profit Hunter' designed to challenge smaller mainline jets.
description: Known as the 'Profit Hunter', the E195-E2 is the largest aircraft built by Embraer. It offers single-aisle mainline capacity with regional jet efficiency and quiet cabin acoustics.
keyFeatures: Lowest fuel burn per seat in the 120–150 seat market
Redesigned Airspace-style luggage bins and lighting
Lowest noise footprint in its size class

name: ATR 42-600
short_description: Short-haul regional turboprop designed for short, unpaved runways and remote destinations.
description: The ATR 42-600 is a twin-turboprop regional airliner tailored for short-haul operations with exceptional STOL (short takeoff and landing) performance. Built by European joint venture ATR, it features modern glass cockpits and high efficiency on low-density routes.
keyFeatures: Excellent short-field and unpaved runway capability
Thales glass cockpit with RNP approach capabilities
High fuel efficiency on short-haul island and mountain routes

name: ATR 72-600
short_description: The world's best-selling regional turboprop, stretched from the ATR 42.
description: Stretched by 4.5 meters over the ATR 42, the ATR 72-600 is the dominant regional turboprop globally. It delivers unmatched economics on short feeder routes, consuming up to 45% less fuel than competing regional jets.
keyFeatures: Rear-door passenger loading with integrated stairs
PW127XT engines delivering lower maintenance costs and fuel burn
Armonia cabin design with wide overhead bins

name: Bombardier CRJ200
short_description: Pioneering 50-seat regional jet derived from the Challenger business jet.
description: Developed from the Challenger 600 corporate jet, the Bombardier CRJ100/200 launched the regional jet boom of the 1990s by replacing slow turboprops on lower-density routes with jet speeds and altitudes.
keyFeatures: Rear fuselage-mounted engine arrangement and T-tail
Fast cruising speeds comparable to mainline jets
Standard 2x2 seating layout

name: Bombardier CRJ700
short_description: Stretched, re-engined regional jet fitted with slatted wings and lower floor height.
description: The CRJ700 stretched the original CRJ chassis, adding a redesigned wing with leading-edge slats, powerful CF34-8C engines, and a lowered cabin floor to increase headroom and window height.
keyFeatures: Leading-edge slats for enhanced takeoff and landing performance
Lower cabin floor level for enlarged passenger headroom
Scope-clause compliant 70-seat configuration

name: Bombardier CRJ900
short_description: 90-seat stretched variant offering high seat-mile efficiency for regional feeders.
description: Further stretching the CRJ700 frame by nearly 4 meters, the CRJ900 added underfloor cargo volume, strengthened landing gear, and higher MTOW options to handle high-density regional routes.
keyFeatures: Stretched airframe with two extra emergency exit doors over the wings
NextGen interior upgrade featuring larger windows and overhead bins
Common type rating with CRJ700 and CRJ1000

name: De Havilland Dash 8 Q400
short_description: High-speed turboprop equipped with Active Noise and Vibration Suppression.
description: The Dash 8 Q400 ('Q' for Quiet) revolutionized turboprop flying by pairing jet-like cruise speeds (up to 360 knots) with active noise-suppression technology inside the cabin, significantly blunting the typical turboprop vibration.
keyFeatures: ANVS (Active Noise and Vibration Suppression) system in cabin
PW150A engines developing over 5,000 shaft horsepower each
High cruise speed approaching regional jet velocity

name: Douglas DC-3
short_description: The transformative piston-powered airliner that made passenger air travel profitable.
description: The Douglas DC-3 is one of the most significant transport aircraft in aviation history. Designed in the 1930s, its reliability, speed, and range made commercial passenger transport economic without government subsidies for the first time.
keyFeatures: Pioneered sustainable commercial airline business models
All-metal cantilever monoplane construction
Unmatched ruggedness with hundreds remaining operational decades after production

name: Douglas DC-8-63
short_description: Douglas' classic four-engine long-range jet designed to rival the Boeing 707.
description: The DC-8 entered service as Douglas' first jetliner. Known for its strong structural design, later 'Super 60' stretched models and re-engined 'Super 70' variants gave it unprecedented payload capacity and long service life as a freighter.
keyFeatures: First passenger jetliner to break the sound barrier in a test dive (1961)
Super 60 stretched fuselage design holding up to 259 passengers
CFM56 re-engine program (Super 70 series) for noise and emissions compliance

name: Douglas DC-9-30
short_description: Highly successful twinjet tailored for short-haul and small airport operations.
description: The DC-9 was designed as a twin-engine short-haul complement to the larger four-engine DC-8. Featuring aft-mounted engines, a T-tail, and built-in airstairs, it allowed airlines to service smaller regional airports without extensive ground support.
keyFeatures: Rear-mounted engines creating a quiet forward cabin
Integrated ventral airstairs for self-sufficient airport turnarounds
5-abreast seating layout

name: McDonnell Douglas DC-10-30
short_description: First wide-body trijet airliner built for medium-to-long range intercontinental routes.
description: The DC-10 was McDonnell Douglas' first wide-body jet, featuring a distinctive straight-through banjo duct layout for its vertical stabilizer engine. The long-range DC-10-30 became a transatlantic and transpacific workhorse.
keyFeatures: Trijet layout with a tail-mounted vertical fin engine
Wide-body cabin with dual aisles
Basis for the USAF KC-10 Extender aerial refueling tanker

name: McDonnell Douglas MD-11
short_description: Advanced long-range wide-body trijet stretched from the DC-10.
description: The MD-11 stretched the DC-10, adding winglets, high-efficiency engines, an extended tail cone, and a 2-crew glass cockpit. While its passenger service was truncated by twinjet ETOPS rivals, it established a long second life as a primary heavy freighter.
keyFeatures: Advanced glass cockpit eliminating the flight engineer role
Upward and downward facing winglets for drag reduction
High cargo capacity favored by global logistics carriers

name: McDonnell Douglas MD-82
short_description: Affectionately known as the 'Mad Dog', second-generation DC-9 derivative.
description: The MD-80 series (originally DC-9 Super 80) featured a stretched fuselage, wider wingspan, and low-bypass JT8D-200 series engines. It formed the backbone of domestic US carrier fleets throughout the 1980s and 1990s.
keyFeatures: Distinctive long narrow fuselage with rear engines
Acoustically quiet forward cabin section
5-abreast seating layout (3x2)

name: McDonnell Douglas MD-90-30
short_description: Quieter, stretched MD-80 derivative equipped with high-bypass IAE V2500 engines.
description: The MD-90 was a modernized development of the MD-80 series featuring high-bypass IAE V2500 turbofans, an EFIS electronic flight instrument cockpit, and an extra 1.4-meter fuselage stretch. It served as the foundation for the Boeing 717 (MD-95).
keyFeatures: Ultra-quiet high-bypass IAE V2500 engines
EFIS glass cockpit flight deck
Predecessor to the Boeing 717

name: L-1011 TriStar
short_description: A technologically advanced tri-jet wide-body airliner featuring an early automated landing system.
description: The Lockheed L-1011 TriStar was a medium-to-long-range, wide-body tri-jet airliner. It was one of the most technologically advanced commercial aircraft of its era, pioneering autoland systems and direct lift control, though intense competition ultimately curtailed commercial production.
keyFeatures: S-duct center engine integration
CAT IIIb automatic landing system
Direct Lift Control (DLC) system
Full-width lower deck galley with elevator

name: Concorde
short_description: The world's most successful supersonic commercial airliner, cruising at Mach 2.02.
description: Concorde was an Anglo-French turbojet-powered supersonic passenger airliner. Operated exclusively by British Airways and Air France, it flew transatlantic routes in under half the time of conventional subsonic jets until its retirement in 2003.
keyFeatures: Ogival delta wing design
Droop-nose visor system for runway visibility
Supercruise capability (Mach 2 without continuous afterburners)
Thermal expansion airframe engineering

name: C909
short_description: China's twin-engine regional jet airliner, originally developed as the ARJ21 and rebranded as the C909.
description: The COMAC C909 (originally launched as the ARJ21 Xiangfeng) is China's first domestically developed regional jet. Designed for short-to-medium routes and high-temperature/high-altitude operations in Western China, it was officially rebranded under COMAC's unified 'C' naming convention in 2024.
keyFeatures: Supercritical wing design with winglets
High-temperature and high-altitude (plateau) operational capability
Rear-mounted engine configuration
Advanced glass cockpit avionics

name: C919
short_description: China's premier narrow-body twinjet designed to compete with the A320neo and 737 MAX.
description: The COMAC C919 is a mainline commercial narrow-body airliner developed by China. Designed to challenge the Airbus A320 family and Boeing 737 family, it features modern aerodynamic design, widespread use of composite materials, and advanced LEAP-1C engines.
keyFeatures: Third-generation aluminum-lithium alloy construction
Side-stick fly-by-wire flight control system
Advanced CFM LEAP-1C high-bypass turbofans
Large 15.4-inch glass cockpit multifunction displays
